title: The AI SaaS Ads Playbook: Oliver Brocato on paid ads, testing, LTV and distribution for SaaS
summary: Oliver Brocato explains how he picks products and channels that fit his edge, borrows proven ideas, and wins paid ads through a strong back-end (LTV, pricing, upsells) and heavy creative testing. He also covers channel-product fit, in-person distribution and super affiliates for his e-commerce brand-protection SaaS.

principles.text: Build in spaces where you hold a distribution edge, and pick products that suit your core skill.
principles.quote: I like to play I like to play in spaces that I have an edge in.

principles.text: Let others validate the market, then improve one thing; existing competitors are signal, not a stop sign.
principles.quote: I think it's important to let other people do the groundwork and the heavy lifting and the validating for you.

principles.text: Ads win on the back-end machine (pricing tests, flows, upsells), not on a copied creative. Higher LTV lets you afford higher CAC.
principles.quote: if I don't have like the machine that you've spent you know years building out. I could run the same ad as you.

principles.text: Scaling ads from six to seven figures comes down to creative and volume testing, then remaking winning angles with many creators and hooks.
principles.quote: in order to scale from like six figures a month to seven figures a month and like really do big boy numbers is it all comes down to like creative testing like and volume testing

principles.text: Test many channels fast, fail quickly, and go all in when one shows a sliver of traction; the product shapes which channel works.
principles.quote: the biggest principles is test test test try try see something that works 100x double down on it and and go all in on it.

principles.text: Recruit a few well-networked super affiliates (agency or software owners); one rolodex can beat ads or cold email.
principles.quote: One guy like that with that kind of a rolodex and book of business is worth like, you know, a lot like way more than like Facebook ads or cold email.
